lesson.text: Remember? A noun names a thing. A verb is a doing or being word: run, think, is.
The tense tells when. Past: yesterday I played. Present: today I play, or I am playing. Future: tomorrow I will play.
Regular verbs add -ed for the past: jump, jumped; walk, walked. Irregular verbs change in their own way: run, ran; swim, swam; take, took; go, went; see, saw; think, thought.
The verb agrees with its subject: one dog barks, two dogs bark. He runs, they run. I am, you are, she is.
The present perfect tells what has happened up to now: "I have finished my book." "She has seen a whale." Use has with he, she and it. Use have with I, you, we and they.
Try it in the world: tell a friend what you did in your world yesterday, what you are doing today and what you will do tomorrow. Check each verb's tense. Next: describing words.

exercises.prompt: What is the past tense of "jump"?
exercises.explain: jump + ed = jumped.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is in the future?
exercises.explain: "Will swim" tells about tomorrow: the future.

exercises.prompt: What is the past tense of "run"?
exercises.explain: Today I run; yesterday I ran.

exercises.prompt: "Walked" is a verb in the past tense.
exercises.explain: True: walked ends in -ed and tells about the past.

exercises.prompt: The dog ___ at the postman.
exercises.hint: One dog: the verb ends in s.
exercises.explain: One dog barks. Two dogs bark.

exercises.prompt: What is the past tense of "take"?
exercises.explain: Today I take; yesterday I took.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is in the past?
exercises.explain: "Wrote" is the past of write.

exercises.prompt: They ___ happy.
exercises.explain: They are. (He is. I am.)

exercises.prompt: What is the past tense of "think"?
exercises.explain: Today I think; yesterday I thought.

exercises.prompt: "She ___ seen a whale." Which word makes the present perfect?
exercises.hint: Use has with he, she and it.
exercises.explain: She has seen a whale.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
choices: The children play in the park.
The children plays in the park.
exercises.explain: More than one: the children play.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses the present perfect?
exercises.hint: Look for has or have with the verb.
exercises.explain: "Have finished" is the present perfect.

exercises.prompt: Put the sentences in time order: past, present, future.
exercises.explain: Past: swam. Present: am swimming. Future: will swim.

exercises.prompt: What is the past tense of "swim"?
exercises.hint: Say it: today I swim; yesterday I… The word changes its middle letter.
exercises.explain: Yesterday I swam. (Swum goes with have: I have swum.)

exercises.prompt: "Goed" is the past tense of "go".
exercises.explain: False: the past of go is went.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb to its past tense.
exercises.hint: Say each pair: today I run, yesterday I ran. Do the same for each verb.
exercises.explain: run, ran; take, took; go, went; see, saw.

exercises.prompt: Sort the verbs: past or present?
exercises.hint: Try 'yesterday' or 'today' in front of each one. Which sounds right?
exercises.explain: Past: jumped, took and saw. Present: runs, swim and thinks.

exercises.prompt: Sort the verbs: regular (add -ed) or irregular?
exercises.hint: Say each one in the past. Does it just add -ed, or does it change?
exercises.explain: Regular: walked, jumped and played. Irregular: go becomes went, see becomes saw, and think becomes thought.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence in the past.
exercises.hint: Start with who did it, then what they did.
exercises.explain: Pip won the race yesterday: who (Pip), the past verb (won), what (the race), then when (yesterday).

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: past, present or future?
exercises.hint: Find the verb in each. Does it say 'will', is it a past form, or is it happening now?
exercises.explain: Past: wrote and went. Present: are playing and think. Future: will swim and will go.
